# Week 3 Start/Sit Briefing — Monday, 2026-09-21

## Source and freshness

**Live** — `nflreadpy` (schedules, rosters, player stats, depth charts) + the repo's fitted `AvailabilityModel`, run end-to-end via `generate_report.py` at 2026-09-21T06:19:45Z. Two real gaps, both stated up front rather than hidden:

- **No Week 3 injury/practice report exists yet anywhere** — `nflreadpy.load_injuries(2026)` only carries weeks 1–2 (this is normal: teams' first Week 3 practice reports post Wednesday, two days from now). Sleeper is proxy-blocked in this sandbox regardless. So every player below is scored on depth-chart rank + play-rate history, not fresh injury news — P(play) is real and live-computed, but "Healthy" designations here mean "nothing to report yet," not "confirmed clean."
- **FantasyPros consensus tier is unavailable** (no `FANTASYPROS_API_KEY` in this sandbox), so Taylor, Irving, JSN and Likely — who'd normally get FantasyPros' vendor number — are instead scored by the in-house rolling-average model on just 2 games of 2026 data. That model is real and live, but it understates established veterans early in a season more than the vendor consensus would. It does **not** change any of tonight's slot-lock decisions (see below), but it does mean the point totals for our top four are conservative.

`season_week.load_current_week_nflreadpy` returns **Week 2** (Week 2's last game, NYG @ LA Monday Night, hasn't been played — it kicks off later today, US time). Consistent with this routine's own Monday cadence (the 2026-09-14 briefing did the same thing while Week 1's Monday-nighter was still pending), this briefing targets **Week 3**, the next lineup decision, and calls out the still-live Week 2 game separately below.

## Start these ten (Week 3)

| Slot | Player | Opp | Expected pts | P(play) | If he plays |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| QB | Jaxson Dart | vs TEN | **13.00** | 91.4% | 14.23 |
| RB | Jonathan Taylor | vs HOU | **9.19** | 93.2% | 9.86 |
| RB | Bucky Irving | vs MIN | **6.80** | 93.2% | 7.29 |
| WR | Jaxon Smith-Njigba | @WAS | **5.46** | 95.5% | 5.72 |
| WR | Jameson Williams | vs NYJ | **3.21** | 84.2% | 3.81 |
| TE | Isaiah Likely | vs TEN | **3.54** | 85.6% | 4.13 |
| FLEX | Cam Skattebo | vs TEN | **6.20** | 86.7% | 7.15 |
| FLEX | Matthew Golden | vs ATL (Thu) | **3.20** | 82.0% | 3.90 |
| K | Cameron Dicker | @BUF | **4.16** | 97.9% | 4.25 |
| DEF | Eagles D/ST | @CHI (Mon 9/28) | **4.73** | 100% | 4.73 |

**Lineup total (expected): 59.49**

**Sit:** Drake London (bench — his 2.72 expected pts is last among the five FLEX-eligible WRs), Tee Higgins (2.78), Josh Downs (2.99), Brock Bowers (2.40, TE2), Matthew Stafford (7.86, QB2 — irrelevant, one QB slot).

## Changes

**One lineup change from the default roster order: bench Drake London, start Jameson Williams, and slide Matthew Golden from a dedicated WR slot into FLEX.** London (2.72 exp pts, @GB Thursday) grades below all three bench WRs — Williams (3.21), Downs (2.99), Higgins (2.78) — and Williams comes out slightly ahead. **Call this low-confidence**: the whole WR2/FLEX2 tier (London/Higgins/Williams/Downs, plus Golden) spans just 0.5 points, on 2 games of data, with no FantasyPros number to check it against. If you'd rather not chase 0.5 points of noise, London-over-Williams is a perfectly defensible hold. Everything else matches how the roster is already ordered.

Since Saturday's briefing (Week 2), the owner also already executed two waiver moves on 2026-09-20 (Harold Fannin Jr. → Isaiah Likely at TE, Quentin Johnston → Matthew Golden at WR) — both are reflected in the roster and in this lineup already, not new decisions from this run.

## Watch list

- **Brock Bowers (TE, LV)** — last confirmed live status was Week 2 Doubtful/knee/Limited practice. No Week 3 report yet; if he's healthier this week it still doesn't threaten Likely's TE spot (Likely is the clear play), but it's the one designation worth re-checking Wednesday since it's chronic.
- **Matthew Golden (WR, GB) vs Drake London (WR, ATL)** — same game, Thursday night (9/24), and they guard each other's fantasy value directly (see Opponent notes). Whichever offense controls that game script moves both numbers.
- **All Week 3 designations** — none exist yet. Re-run Wednesday for the first real practice-report read, which is also when the London/Williams FLEX call gets its first real evidence beyond the rolling average.
- **Bills D/ST** projects at 6.36 this week (vs our Eagles D/ST's 4.73) in the in-house model and may be worth a waiver look if available in-league — not acted on here since roster availability across the other 7 teams isn't visible from this run.

## Opponent notes

- **Golden (GB) and London (ATL) play each other Thursday night** — GB hosts ATL. A tough Packers front for Atlanta's offense is part of why London grades lowest of the FLEX-eligible WRs this week; conversely Golden's Green Bay offense at home is the more favorable side of that same game.
- **Three rostered Giants — Dart, Skattebo, Likely — all play TEN this week.** That's correlated risk: a poor Giants game script (trailing big, run-heav's abandoned) would flatten all three at once, whereas a positive script lifts the whole trio together. Worth knowing you can't diversify away from this one.
- **Taylor and Downs share an opponent** (both IND, vs HOU) — no lineup implication since both are already rostered appropriately (Taylor starts, Downs sits), just noted for completeness.

## Byes ahead

**None in the next two weeks (Weeks 3–4).** Nearest byes: **Tee Higgins and Jameson Williams, both Week 6** — three weeks out. Both are currently bench/flex-competitive WRs, so if either is traded up into a lock-in role before Week 6, plan a waiver replacement early rather than relying on the thin bench (5 spots, already carrying a QB2, a TE2, and 3 WRs).

## Caveats

- No live Week 3 injury/practice data exists anywhere yet (confirmed via `nflreadpy.load_injuries`, which caps at Week 2) — every "Healthy" designation above means "nothing reported," not "cleared." Re-run Wednesday for the real read, especially on Bowers.
- FantasyPros consensus tier unavailable in this sandbox (no API key) — Taylor/Irving/JSN/Likely's expected-points numbers are the more conservative in-house estimate, not the vendor consensus this tool normally uses for top-10-per-position players. Their starting slots aren't in question either way.
- ESPN's and Rotowire's endpoints are proxy-blocked in this sandbox (expected, per known network reality); Sleeper likewise. No opponent-news layer beyond the schedule/matchup facts stated above.
- The Williams-over-London call is a ~0.5-point edge on 2 games of data — treat it as a coin flip, not a strong signal.
- Week 2's final game (NYG @ LA, Monday Night) had not been played as of this run; it does not affect this Week 3 lineup, since all three Giants already start regardless of tonight's outcome.
